summary: ARES, the federation of higher education institutions in French-speaking Belgium, gives scholarships for people from 32 partner countries to take a specialised bachelor, a one-year specialised master or a six-month continuing-training course at institutions of the Wallonia-Brussels Federation. The courses focus on development-related issues and are meant for working professionals who will return to their institution or profession. The scholarship pays for international travel, a monthly subsistence allowance and insurance, plus other items depending on the level.
eligibility_notes:
Applicants must be permanent residents of one of the 32 partner countries and work there. Palestinian nationals may apply even if they do not live in one of the 32 countries. Eligibility depends on residence and work, not on passport. The countries are Benin, Bolivia, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cambodia, Cameroon, Cuba, Democratic Republic of Congo, Ecuador, Ethiopia, Haiti, Indonesia, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Madagascar, Mali, Morocco, Mozambique, Nepal, Niger, Palestine, Peru, Philippines, Republic of Guinea (Conakry), Rwanda, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania, Tunisia, Uganda, Vietnam and Zimbabwe.

The applicant must hold a higher education qualification and meet the admission requirements of the chosen course. The relevant degree may be at most 20 years old when the course begins; this limit is extended by one year for each childbirth or adoption.

The applicant must show at least two years of relevant professional experience in one of the 32 countries after the last higher education qualification (after a bachelor for the specialised bachelor, after a master for specialised masters and continuing education).

The application form must be completed in the language of the course, and the applicant must be able to show good written and spoken knowledge of it. A little French helps with daily life in Belgium. Only one course may be applied for. Previous admission to a French-speaking Belgian institution is not needed before applying.

People who already received an ARES scholarship in Belgium are not eligible. Meeting the criteria does not guarantee selection. Incomplete applications or those without the mandatory attachments are not followed up. Applying is free; ARES says it never charges fees at any stage.
age_experience_notes: No age limit is stated. The relevant degree must be no more than 20 years old at course start (plus one year per childbirth or adoption). At least two years of relevant professional experience in an eligible country after the last degree is required; some courses ask for more or set their own experience rules (for example the public health master asks for at least two years in public health, and the preventive conservation master asks for two years in a heritage institution).
funding_summary: For the specialised bachelor and specialised masters the scholarship covers one return economy flight per academic year, a monthly subsistence allowance for 12 months (plus a reduced 13th month), visa-related charges (up to a set amount) and insurance paid directly by ARES, and the call page also lists tuition fees. Continuing training gets a return flight, a monthly allowance for the length of the course, a fixed sum for extra travel-related fees and insurance. Funding lasts one academic year (September to June or September) for bachelor and masters, and 6 months for continuing training.
programmes_note: Ten courses are offered: one specialised bachelor, eight specialised masters and one continuing-training certificate. Each has its own entry conditions in a presentation document on the ARES site. Most courses have 10 scholarships; the human rights master has 11.
institutions_note: Courses are run by institutions of the Wallonia-Brussels Federation: EPHEC (bachelor); ULiège, ULB, UNamur, UCLouvain, UMONS, HEPL and ENSAV La Cambre (masters), in different combinations per course. The applicant picks one course; the course's academic jury selects among candidates.

summary.detail: One specialised bachelor: Digital Integrated Supply Chain, 60 ECTS in 12 months, taught in French, 10 scholarships. Meant to complete a professional bachelor or master from economics and management, or computer science. Admission by VAE (recognition of experience) is possible with at least 5 years of related experience, an assessment test and an admission jury decision.

programmes.name: Specialised Bachelor in Digital Integrated Supply Chain (DISC)
programmes.institution: Haute École EPHEC (lead) with École Supérieure EPHEC de Promotion sociale
programmes.detail: One academic year, French, 10 scholarships; lists accepted bachelor and master titles in domain 9 (economics and management) and domain 17 (computer science)

summary.detail: Eight specialised or advanced masters of one academic year, in French except the economics and microfinance masters which are in English. Applicants need a degree that meets the course's admission rules and at least two years of relevant professional experience after their master (call document).

programmes.name: Specialised Master in Human Rights (Master de spécialisation en droits humains)
programmes.detail: One year, French (one elective in English); 11 scholarships; entry with a 120-credit second-cycle degree in law or a related field, with outstanding studies or substantial human-rights experience; very good French and passive English needed

programmes.name: Specialised Master in Integrated Management of Health Risks
programmes.detail: One year, French with possible exceptions for international speakers; passive English required; 10 scholarships

programmes.name: Specialised Master in International and Development Economics (SMIDE)
programmes.detail: One year, English; 10 scholarships; entry with a degree after 5 years of university study, or after 4 years plus at least 2 years of professional experience; sufficient background in economics; a written test in some cases; classes start 15 September 2027

programmes.name: Advanced Master in Microfinance
programmes.detail: One year, English; 10 scholarships; second-cycle degree or substantial professional experience; English proof (TOEFL, IELTS, Cambridge FCE or CAE grade C) unless exempt

programmes.name: Specialised Master in Public Health Sciences: analysis and evaluation of international health policies, programmes and systems
programmes.detail: One year, 60 credits, French with passive English; 10 scholarships; needs public health basics, a health, social or economics master, 2 years of public health experience, motivation letter, one-page case; video interview for the shortlist

programmes.name: Specialised Master in Food Chain Safety Management (MASCA)
programmes.institution: ULiège Faculty of Veterinary Medicine, Haute École de la Province de Liège
programmes.detail: One year, French; 10 scholarships; direct access for holders of masters such as veterinary medicine, medicine, pharmaceutical sciences, biomedical sciences, bioengineering and others, other profiles by jury decision

programmes.name: Specialised Master in Preventive Conservation and Collection Management
programmes.detail: One year, French; 10 scholarships; second-cycle degree in conservation-restoration, art history, archaeology, museology or heritage management, and 2 years in a heritage institution; interview

programmes.name: Specialised Master in Risk and Disaster Management in the Anthropocene
programmes.detail: One year, mainly French (one course and some seminars may be in English); 10 scholarships

summary.detail: One continuing-training certificate lasting up to 6 months: Certificate in Cybersecurity Operations and Risk Governance. Participants need a master and two years of professional experience; benefits differ from the bachelor and masters (no tuition or visa line on the call page, a fixed sum for extra travel fees, indirect mission costs).

requirements.text: Certified copies of the original diplomas.
Certified copies of the original transcripts for all years.
Proof of employment (occupancy) for the last 5 years.
Certificate of nationality, national identity card (a voter registration card is not accepted) or a copy of the passport.
Proof of residence: residence certificate, resident card or resident permit. If no such document exists in the country of residence, a signed declaration on honour.
A commitment from the employer to re-employ the applicant after the course.
Pre-project, for certain courses only; see each course's admission conditions.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only for courses that require it

requirements.text: Proof of English where the course sets it (the microfinance master accepts TOEFL, IELTS, Cambridge FCE or CAE grade C, or a certificate that earlier studies were taught in English; native speakers of listed countries need none).
Motivation letter and a one-page description of a work case (public health master).

application_steps.title: Create or reactivate an account on the ARES platform
application_steps.detail: Applicants first need an active account on the ARES online platform (GIRAF). Complete the profile, wait for ARES to validate it (a few hours to a few days, one account only) and use the email address you registered because all official messages go there. New accounts stop two weeks before the deadline; an account unused for two years must be created again.

application_steps.title: Open the form from the competitive calls tab
application_steps.detail: Study the chosen course's admission conditions first. Open the international training form from the Competitive Calls tab (click once), then find it again under My Tasks. Only one course can be applied for.

application_steps.title: Fill in the form, upload documents and save drafts
application_steps.detail: Complete the compulsory fields marked with an asterisk before the first save, and use the save-as-draft option each time (including after each upload) because there is no automatic saving. Attach the eight listed documents; applications that are incomplete or lack mandatory attachments are not followed up. For the 2027-2028 call the closing time was noon Belgian time on the closing day.

application_steps.title: Submit the application for good
application_steps.detail: Check all fields and uploads, then use the final submit button. After that nobody can edit the form and it moves to the submitted applications list; that list is the confirmation even if no email arrives.

application_steps.title: Pre-selection and academic jury assessment
application_steps.detail: For each course an academic jury assesses applications on eight criteria: academic career quality; previous ARES scholarships (past holders are not eligible); professional experience in development-related work; working in an ARES partner institution (tie-breaker); potential to be an agent of change; geographic diversity; gender parity; and the personal and professional ability to pass on the knowledge, including guarantees of return and reintegration such as a work contract or formal promise of employment. Some courses add interviews (video interview for public health, interview for preventive conservation) or a written test (economics, in some cases).

application_steps.title: Results by email
application_steps.detail: The selection runs from October 2026 to May 2027. By June 2027 at the latest ARES emails successful and reserve candidates, and separately unsuccessful candidates. ARES gives no other information, and any appeal against the decision goes to the Council of State.

application_steps.title: Return and reintegration expectations
application_steps.detail: ARES expects the scholar to go back to the home country, or another country, and to be reintegrated into a profession where the training is used for development, backed by an employer re-employment commitment submitted with the application. The course runs for one academic year (September to June or September), or about 6 months for continuing training; some courses start with preparatory distance sessions (for example the economics master from a home country in distance mode, then an orientation in the first weeks of September 2027).
